drills.q: True or false: Trino stores table data locally on worker disks like a database.
drills.a: False -- Trino is stateless between queries; all data lives in source systems accessed through connectors, and workers only hold transient query state in memory/disk scratch.

drills.q: Which component assigns splits to workers and enforces query memory limits?
drills.a: The coordinator -- it schedules splits, aggregates per-worker memory reports continuously, and kills queries that breach user-memory limits (EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT).

drills.q: Your federated Postgres dashboard query ships 40M rows per refresh. Name the first two things you check.
drills.a: 1) EXPLAIN: does the WHERE clause appear inside the Postgres connector's table handle (pushdown) or as a filter above the scan? 2) Does the filtered column have an index on the Postgres side? Pushdown without an index still scans remotely.

drills.q: Query fails with EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT naming a hash join operator. Give the ordered fix list.
drills.a: 1) Gather/refresh table statistics; 2) force PARTITIONED join or cap join.broadcast-threshold if broadcast picked an underestimated side; 3) reduce input cardinality earlier in the plan; 4) enable spill so pressure becomes revocable; 5) raise limits last -- limits are isolation against cluster-wide OOM, not an inconvenience.

drills.q: Why does 'it worked with LIMIT 10' prove nothing about the un-LIMITed query?
drills.a: LIMIT returns early while stages keep running client-side, but blocking operators (hash join build, full aggregation, ORDER BY) must consume entire inputs before emitting -- the full query's memory profile is invisible to the LIMIT run.

drills.q: BI runs five federated dashboards hourly against Aurora. Federation or copy? Defend briefly.
drills.a: Copy: hourly refreshes re-transfer the same rows ~120x/day and put analytical load on an OLTP primary. A scheduled incremental sync into Iceberg amortizes transfer once and removes OLTP exposure, costing one pipeline to own instead of per-query network tax.

drills.q: What changes about running multi-hour batch SQL on Trino once fault-tolerant execution is enabled?
drills.a: Worker loss no longer restarts the whole query: stage intermediates persist to the exchange manager (S3/HDFS) and only lost splits retry. This moves long batch transforms out of Spark's monopoly -- at the price of exchange IO overhead and enabling the exchange manager.

drills.q: An Athena bill doubles month over month. First three checks?
drills.a: 1) Scanned-bytes by query/user via Athena API (find new full scans); 2) dashboards that switched from partition-pruned patterns to full-table patterns; 3) format regression (raw JSON/CSV replacing Parquet). Cost incidents are scan-discipline incidents at $5/TB.

drills.q: Design rule-of-thumb: which joins belong on Spark instead of Trino?
drills.a: Skew-heavy, multi-TB shuffles with long tails -- Spark's AQE skew-partition splitting is mature where Trino's handling stays coarser; also ML/UDF-heavy pipelines and streaming. Trino keeps interactive/light-ELT and federation workloads.
